Anyone using a keyboard, switch or voice control needs to see which control is active. A removed or invisible focus ring leaves them guessing where the next Enter press lands.
Style :focus-visible with a 2px outline in a colour that holds 3:1 against the page and the control, offset a couple of pixels.
Remove the outline with outline:none unless a stronger replacement indicator is drawn in the same rule.
The focus indicator is a user interface component state, so it needs at least 3:1 contrast against the neighbouring colours. A pale blue ring on white fails.
Check the ring against both the page and the control it surrounds; use a two-tone ring (dark inner, light outer) on mixed backgrounds.
Pick a ring colour by eye on one background and assume it works on cards, images and dark sections.
Focus Not Hidden Behind Sticky Bars
A fixed header, cookie bar or chat bubble can cover the element that just received keyboard focus, so the user tabs into something they cannot see.
Give the scroll container scroll-padding equal to the height of the fixed bars, and test by tabbing through the whole page.
Pin bars over content without reserving space for focused elements.
Keyboard users move through the DOM order. If the visual layout and the source order disagree, focus jumps around the screen in a way nobody predicts.
Write the markup in the order people read it and let CSS grid or flex place it; leave tabindex at 0 or -1 only.
Use positive tabindex values or CSS order to reshuffle interactive elements.
Keyboard navigation must reach every action a mouse can: Tab, Enter, Space and arrow keys. Clickable divs are invisible to the keyboard and to assistive tech.
Use button for actions and a for navigation; they bring focus, Enter and Space handling for free.
Attach click handlers to div or span and add role and key handlers by hand.
If focus enters a widget such as an embedded player or editor, the user must be able to leave it with standard keys. A trap forces them to reload.
Test every embed and custom widget by tabbing in and out; document Escape or a dedicated exit key when one is needed.
Capture Tab inside a component with no way out except the mouse.
Keyboard users should not tab through twenty header links on every page. A skip link is the first focusable element and jumps past repeated blocks.
Put an anchor to #main first in the body, visually hidden until focused, and give main that id.
Hide the skip link with display:none, which removes it from the tab order.
Screen reader users jump between landmarks to scan a page. Header, nav, main and footer elements expose that structure without extra attributes.
Use one main, a nav per link group with a distinguishing label, and header and footer at page level.
Build the page from anonymous divs, or use two main elements.
The title is the first thing a screen reader announces and the label on the browser tab and history. Identical titles make pages indistinguishable.
Lead with the page's own subject, then the site name; update the title on every route change in a single-page app.
Ship one title for the whole site, or leave 'Untitled' or 'Home' on inner pages.
Screen readers pick a pronunciation engine from the lang attribute, and browsers use it for hyphenation, quotes and translation prompts.
Set lang on the html element to the real language, with region where it matters.
Leave lang off or copy en from a template onto a page written in another language.
A passage in another language read with the page's voice is gibberish. A lang attribute on the span or block fixes the pronunciation.
Wrap foreign phrases and quotations in an element with the matching lang value.
Leave a French or Welsh phrase inside English text with no marker.
Headings are a navigation list for assistive tech users. Levels should nest by meaning, not by font size.
One h1 per page, h2 for sections, h3 beneath them; restyle with CSS to change the look.
Pick h4 because it looks smaller, or skip from h1 to h4.
Body text needs 4.5:1 against its background and large text (24px, or 19px bold) needs 3:1. Pale grey on white is the most common failure.
Measure the real pair with a contrast tool, including text over images and on hover and disabled-looking states that still carry meaning.
Judge contrast by eye on a bright monitor, or put text straight on a photo.
Borders of inputs, icons that carry meaning and chart marks must reach 3:1 against what is next to them, or people with low vision cannot find them.
Give form field borders, toggles and meaningful icons a 3:1 edge or fill.
Use a 1px light grey border on a white form so the field fades away.
Colour Is Never the Only Signal
Roughly one in twelve men has a colour vision difference. Red and green alone cannot tell them what failed or what passed.
Pair colour with an icon, text label, pattern or underline.
Mark errors by turning a border red and nothing else.
An image that carries meaning needs a text equivalent that gives the same information, not a description of its pixels.
Write alt for the purpose: what the reader would miss without it. Keep it a phrase or a sentence.
Start with 'image of', paste a filename, or stuff keywords.
Pure decoration read aloud is noise. An empty alt attribute tells assistive tech to skip the image.
Use alt='' on decoration, or set it as a CSS background.
Omit alt entirely, which makes some readers announce the file name.
A button that shows just an icon has no accessible name unless you supply one. Voice-control users also need a name they can say.
Add visible text, or aria-label that matches what sighted users infer; hide the svg itself from the tree.
Ship an icon button with no text or label.
Screen reader users often pull up a list of links. 'Click here' and 'Read more' repeated ten times is an unusable list.
Make the link text meaningful alone, or add visually hidden text that completes it.
Voice control users say what they see. If the aria-label differs from the visible text, the spoken command fails.
Start the accessible name with the exact visible words.
Show 'Book now' and set aria-label to 'Reserve an appointment'.
People enlarge text in the browser. Layouts built on fixed pixel heights clip or overlap once text doubles.
Size type in rem and let containers grow with min-height, not height.
Fix heights in px on text containers, or block zoom.
At 400 percent zoom a desktop window behaves like a 320px screen. Content must stack in one column without sideways scrolling, apart from maps, tables and similar two-dimensional content.
Test at 320px width and at 400% zoom; use fluid grids and wrap long strings.
Set min-width on the page or wrapper bigger than a phone.
Some readers override line height, letter and word spacing. Content must remain readable with no clipped text when they do.
Use unitless line-height and let boxes grow; test with a spacing bookmarklet.
Clip text with overflow:hidden in a box of set height.
Hover and Focus Content Is Dismissible
A tooltip or popover that appears on hover must be dismissible with Escape, stay put while the pointer moves onto it, and remain until the user is done.
Let Escape close it, keep it open while hovered or focused, and show it on keyboard focus too.
Show a tooltip only on mouse hover and remove it the moment the pointer drifts.
Toasts, 'item added' notes and result counts appear without moving focus, so a screen reader says nothing unless the region is live.
Render messages into an existing role='status' (polite) or role='alert' (urgent) container.
Inject a new element with the text and expect it to be read.
When a modal opens, focus must move into it, stay inside while it is open, and return to the trigger when it closes.
Use dialog.showModal(), which traps focus and handles Escape, and restore focus to the opener on close.
Show a div over the page and leave focus behind it.
Parallax, large slides and zooms can trigger dizziness or nausea for people with vestibular conditions. The operating system exposes a preference.
Wrap large movement in a prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference query, or replace it with a short fade.
Ignore the setting and animate everything.
Anything that moves for over five seconds beside other content, such as carousels, tickers and animated backgrounds, needs a visible way to pause it.
Provide a real pause button and stop auto-advance on hover and focus.
Auto-rotate a hero with no controls.
A form that silently expires costs people with slower input their work. Time limits need a warning and a way to extend.
Warn at least 20 seconds ahead with a simple extend action, and save drafts.
Log the user out mid-form without notice.
Content that flashes more than three times in a second can trigger seizures. There is no safe visual style that does it.
Keep any flashing below that threshold, and check video and GIF content before publishing.
Use strobe-style transitions or flashing alerts.
Pointer targets should be at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or have enough spacing around smaller ones. Small close icons and tag buttons miss this most.
Pad the hit area with min-width and min-height of 24px (44px for primary actions on touch).
Shrink icons to 14px with no padding.
Pinch, multi-finger swipe and path drawing are hard or impossible for people using a stylus, head pointer or tremor. A tap-based alternative must exist.
Add plus and minus buttons beside pinch-zoom and arrow buttons beside swipe.
Offer zoom or navigation only through a two-finger gesture.
Sortable lists, sliders and file drop zones that only work by dragging exclude many users. Provide a click or keyboard path to the same result.
Offer move up and move down buttons, or a select-then-place flow.
Firing on pointer-down gives no chance to cancel a slip. Letting the user slide off before release prevents accidental activation.
Use click (fires on up) rather than mousedown or touchstart for actions.
Single-key Shortcuts Can Be Turned Off
One-letter shortcuts collide with speech input, which can fire them while the user is dictating. They must be disableable or remappable, or only act when the component has focus.
Scope shortcuts to the focused widget, or require a modifier key.
Bind bare letters at the window level.
Some people mount a tablet in one fixed orientation. Forcing portrait or landscape makes the app unusable for them unless the order is essential.
Support both orientations and test layouts rotated.
Lock the screen to one orientation by default.
